tasks.short: Monitor molding operation and correct problems

steps.what: Check the current product specifications and permitted adjustment limits
Observe continuous operation and inspect products for jams or defects
Determine whether a safe adjustment or stop is necessary
Stop or adjust the machine using the prescribed safe procedure
Verify the response against actual machine behaviour and product condition

tasks.design: Link the current job to its controlled specification and adjustment limits in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}. Only reference navigation changes; observing products, detecting jams, deciding and making safe adjustments remain with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: An operator may have to find the current limits in a separate instruction pack.
tasks.enabler_now: Native job-to-document links can remove part of that lookup.
tasks.still_hard: A jam, material problem or developing defect may not be represented by a single sensor value.
tasks.human_edge: The operator combines sound, movement and product appearance with machine experience.
tasks.altitude: No change in operating authority; a very small lookup saving is possible.

reach.role: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers

evidence.claim: Native job-document links can shorten specification lookup, but do not replace physical monitoring or adjustment.

assumptions: Boundary includes reference lookup, physical observation, response choice, adjustment and verification. Routine measurement recording is counted once in10184; no extra monitoring log is invented here.

Engineering produces controlled specification revision and permitted limits. The operator checks job identifier and revision in s1, whose8 retained hours include the check. Missing or conflicting references require manual retrieval.
Test native document links before code. There is no new machine-control, out-of-range alert, sensor classifier or autonomous adjustment action.
Existing automatic machine runtime is not counted as labour saving. The0.5-hour allowance covers broken reference links.
unknowns: Current reference lookup frequency and native job links
research_questions: Do native links remove any actual lookup time when instructions are already at the machine?

tasks.short: Determine molding setup and production sequence

steps.what: Retrieve the current specifications, blueprints and work orders
Interpret setup, temperature and cycle-time requirements for the material and tooling
Plan the production sequence around tooling, material and job constraints
Write the required settings and sequence on the existing setup sheet

tasks.design: Use native job-document links and the existing setup-sheet form in {OPS_SYSTEM}, with controlled sources in {DOCS}. Reuse stable job and tooling references, while the operator interprets the requirements, chooses the sequence and writes the actual settings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document revisions and stable setup identifiers are repeatedly found and copied.
tasks.enabler_now: Native job packs and setup forms may remove that retrieval and repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: Material behaviour and tooling constraints can make an apparently similar setup unsuitable.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognizes when a prior setup does not apply to the current material or tool.
tasks.altitude: Less job-pack handling leaves more time to check setup compatibility.

reach.role: Multiple Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic

evidence.claim: Native job packs and setup forms can reduce document retrieval and repeated identifiers; the molding-specific design and time estimate are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is source review, setup interpretation, sequence planning and the actual setup sheet used for the job. Physical machine setup is separate and is not claimed as a saving.

Engineering produces revision-controlled drawings and specification limits; planning produces the work order. The operator checks job, revision, material, tooling, temperature unit and cycle-time unit in s1-s2 and writes required values in s4. Retained14 retrieval and14 writing hours include checks and capture. Missing units or conflicts require manual clarification.
Test native job packs and forms before code. No automatically calculated molding recipe, machine-setting upload or production-release send is introduced.
The author's ordinary setup-sheet save has no approval gate or saving. The sheet is an existing operating artefact, not an added trailing record.
unknowns: Whether the current setup sheet can reuse stable references
research_questions: Do native packs reduce retrieval without hiding revision or material differences?

steps.what: Observe meters and gauges and establish the actual readings
Verify temperatures, pressures and press-cycle times against the required conditions
Record the readings, units and observation time in the process log

tasks.design: Use the existing process-log form in {OPS_SYSTEM} with stable job, machine and unit headings selected once for the run. The operator still reads the actual gauges, verifies the conditions and enters and checks each measurement; no sensor feed or automatic out-of-range alert is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper entries repeat job references, unit headings and time formatting around each actual reading.
tasks.enabler_now: A native repeated-measurement form may remove stable-field handwriting while retaining value capture.
tasks.still_hard: An entered value can be wrong even when its format is valid.
tasks.human_edge: The operator notices a sticking gauge, implausible trend or changing process condition.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated heading entry leaves more attention for reading accuracy.

reach.learn: Units, observation time and instrument checks

evidence.claim: MPDV HYDRA X supports machine quantities and statuses through machine capture or manual entry; this supports manual record-entry capability, not an existing temperature or pressure feed.
The molding measurement-form configuration and retained-time estimate are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual gauge observation, condition verification and the required measurement record. Adjusting a machine is counted in10173 rather than duplicated here.

The operator produces temperature, pressure, cycle time, units and observation time from actual gauges in s1 and verifies them in s2. The operator captures machine, job and values in s3;35 observation hours,25 verification hours and20 retained recording hours include all source capture and checking. Missing or unreliable readings use manual investigation and the current log.
Test native measurement forms before code. No structured discrepancy code, sensor status or unproduced timestamp is assumed; the observation time is entered and checked by the operator.
Same-system author saving has no self-approval stage or saving. No automatic measurement commit, alert or external send is proposed.
unknowns: Current share of repeated headings versus actual value entry

steps.what: Check the operation's attachment specification and tool references
Select compatible blades, tools or attachments and inspect their condition
Isolate the machine and prepare safe access
Install and secure the selected attachment
Verify attachment security, clearance and readiness using the prescribed checks

tasks.design: Link the current operation to its attachment references in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}. Selection, condition inspection, isolation, fitting and readiness checks remain physical work; no automatic tool selection or machine actuation is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attachment references may be found in a separate instruction pack.
tasks.enabler_now: A native operation-reference link may shorten that lookup.
tasks.still_hard: The correct reference does not prove that the actual attachment is undamaged or safely fitted.
tasks.human_edge: The operator detects wear, poor seating and a clearance problem during installation.
tasks.altitude: A very small reference saving is possible; installation responsibility stays the same.

Engineering produces operation revision and permitted attachment identifiers. The operator checks those references in s1, whose12 retained hours include the check, and confirms actual identity and condition in s2. Missing or conflicting references require manual clarification.
Test native links before code. There is no free compatibility flag, automated tool change, new release commit or external send.
The0.5-hour upkeep allowance covers reference-link corrections; physical installation and readiness checks remain fully counted.
unknowns: Whether attachment references are already at the machine
